headline: K2 GOLD DRILLS 95m AT 3.11 g/t AND 84m AT 3.40 g/t FROM SURFACE — Phase 1 Finale at Dragonfly Confirms Bulk-Tonnage Oxide Gold System in Yukon
snippet: K2 Gold (TSXV: KTO) closed out Phase 1 at its Dragonfly zone in Yukon with four final holes including DF26-032 at 95 metres grading 3.11 g/t Au and DF26-031 at 83.82 metres grading 3.40 g/t Au — both from surface — with a 19.81-metre high-grade core in DF26-031 returning 7.51 g/t Au. Phase 1 totals 42 holes and 8,013 metres of a fully funded 14,000-metre program, and the consistent near-surface, wide-step results across Dragonfly are building the geometry needed for a bulk-tonnage oxide gold resource estimate — the type of asset that has attracted royalty companies and mid-tier acquirers at $4,000+ gold.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD HITS 7.88 g/t OVER 12.70m AT GOLD ROCK — 46 g/t High-Grade Core Confirmed in Latest Ontario Assay Batch
snippet: Dryden Gold (TSXV: DRY) intersected 7.88 g/t gold over 12.70 metres including a 1.90-metre section at 46.05 g/t Au at its Gold Rock Camp in Ontario — the latest high-grade result from a project that has now returned visible gold and bonanza-grade cores in multiple holes. The company has deployed a second drill rig at Gold Rock to systematically test the down-plunge depth extension at 100-metre steps, with the system open at depth and along strike in a jurisdiction where similar high-grade shear-hosted discoveries have attracted royalty interest or been absorbed into major portfolios at this exploration stage.

headline: NINE MILE METALS DRILLS 7.13% COPPER EQUIVALENT OVER 11.65m AT WEDGE — New Brunswick VMS Delivers Phase 3 High-Grade Confirmation
snippet: Nine Mile Metals (CSE: NINE) reported that drill hole DDH WD-26-18 at its Wedge VMS project in New Brunswick returned 7.13% copper equivalent over 11.65 metres — including sub-intervals of 9.93% and 10.46% CuEq — alongside a 31.50-metre copper stringer zone, the Phase 3 program's best result. The Bathurst Mining Camp hosts some of the world's most prolific historic VMS deposits, and at Phase 3's conclusion the company expects to publish an updated NI 43-101 technical report incorporating three years of drilling — the document that will allow the market to put a proper dollar value on what looks increasingly like a high-grade copper discovery.

headline: METALS COMPLEX HAMMERED HEADING INTO FOMC WEEK — Gold Retests $4,000 Floor as Copper Posts Sharpest Weekly Drop in Five Weeks
snippet: Gold retested the critical $4,000 per ounce support level on October 22 while copper posted its largest weekly decline in five weeks, compressing margins across the junior mining complex in the week before the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. Mining equities tracked spot prices lower with outsized leverage, and the gold-silver ratio remains near 73 — historically elevated and a potential setup for sharp silver outperformance once the Fed removes uncertainty. For retail investors holding junior positions, the FOMC catalyst on October 28 is the most significant near-term event in the metals calendar.

headline: METALS EXPLORATION RESUMES LA INDIA MINE CONSTRUCTION — Work Restarts in Nicaragua After Fatal Oct 19 Site Incident
snippet: AIM-listed Metals Exploration (LON: MTL) confirmed it has resumed construction activities at its La India gold project in Nicaragua after suspending work following a fatal workplace incident on October 19, 2026. With the process plant more than 80% complete, the full $27 million equipment loan drawn in September, and first gold production targeted for December 2026, the restart keeps one of the more closely watched AIM gold development timelines on track — though the incident will likely draw investor scrutiny to the company's safety management protocols at a critical final-sprint construction phase.

headline: ARAFURA RARE EARTHS REPLACES CHAIR WITH IAN MURRAY — Leadership Transition at Australia's Largest Undeveloped NdPr Project
snippet: Arafura Rare Earths (ASX: ARU) has appointed Ian Murray as non-executive chairman, replacing Mark Southey, as the company continues to navigate the project financing for its Nolans NdPr operation in the Northern Territory. Arafura's 98,000-tonne NdPr oxide resource is one of the largest globally, but closing the A$1.6 billion development capital structure has proved challenging in the current rare earth price environment — and the chair change introduces new board-level energy at a company whose financing timeline is a key variable for anyone tracking Australia's domestic rare earths supply chain ambitions.

headline: HAWTHORN RESOURCES MOVES TO RESTART MINING AT ANGLO SAXON — 200koz at 4.1 g/t Goldfields JV Shifts from Studies to Execution
snippet: Hawthorn Resources (ASX: HAW) is advancing plans to recommence open-pit gold mining at its Anglo Saxon joint venture project in the WA Goldfields, supported by a January 2026 updated mineral resource of 1.53 million tonnes at 4.1 g/t gold for approximately 200,000 ounces. The project sits 140 kilometres northeast of Kalgoorlie within reach of established processing infrastructure, and at $4,000+ gold the economics of a conventional open-pit operation at 4.1 g/t grade are materially stronger than when the mine last operated — giving Hawthorn a rare near-term catalyst in a market starved of advanced-stage, low-capital Australian gold stories.

headline: ALPHA EXPLORATION WRAPS ENLARGED ABURNA DRILL PROGRAM — Ethiopia Gold Project Expands Beyond 2026 Plan Ahead of Resource Estimate
snippet: Alpha Exploration (TSXV: ALEX) has completed an enlarged 2026 drill program at its Aburna gold project in Ethiopia after early results justified expanding beyond the originally planned scope. Assays from the additional holes are pending, with a resource estimate expected to follow — setting up a potential re-rating event for a company that trades at a deep discount to its exploration potential. Aburna sits in Ethiopia's underexplored Arabian-Nubian Shield belt, a geological setting that has hosted major discoveries in neighbouring Sudan and Eritrea, and the expanded dataset could support a maiden or significantly upgraded resource number.

headline: CANAGOLD REPORTS HIGH-GRADE RESULTS FROM NEW POLARIS — Historic British Columbia Gold Mine's 2026 Program Advances Pre-Feasibility Case
snippet: Canagold Resources (TSXV) released new high-grade drill results from its New Polaris gold project in northwestern British Columbia, building on a 2026 program targeting conversion of inferred resources to the measured and indicated categories needed for a pre-feasibility study. New Polaris is a bonanza-grade historic producer in BC's Golden Triangle fringe — a jurisdiction where proximity to established infrastructure and demonstrated high-grade continuity have underpinned several significant royalty and acquisition transactions at lower gold prices than today's $4,000+ market.

headline: AURIGINAL MINING HITS 45.5m GOLD INTERCEPT AT ROGER — Ontario Drill Program Intersects Wide Gold at Shallow Depths
snippet: Auriginal Mining reported a 45.5-metre gold intercept at its Roger project in Ontario, adding width and confidence to the emerging gold system at a depth range accessible to conventional open-pit mining methods. The result comes during an active Ontario junior exploration season where elevated gold prices and a well-developed provincial regulatory framework are attracting increased drill activity — and wide, shallow intercepts in the Ontario Shield tend to attract early-stage acquisition interest from royalty companies and mid-tier producers looking to add resource ounces at below-development-cost prices.
